extracted.intended_audience: corporate counsel, in-house IP teams, and companies seeking ITC Section 337 representation; IP litigators evaluating ITC practice capabilities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit evaluation criteria for representing parties (complainants or respondents) in U.S. International Trade Commission Section 337 patent investigations, including litigation strategy, customs-stage enforcement, and coordination with parallel proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized approach and deep knowledge of ITC
rubrics_metrics.description: Successfully navigating a Section 337 investigation before the ITC requires both extensive IP litigation experience and deep, firsthand knowledge of how the ITC works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that the ITC is governed by a unique statutory scheme and 'calls for a very specialized approach' to defending IP. Select counsel who demonstrate detailed procedural and substantive familiarity with ITC practice rather than general patent litigation experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Section 337 jurisdictional scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 prohibits unfair methods of competition (including patent infringement) in connection with products imported, or sold for importation, into the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statutory scope to evaluate whether an alleged injury fits ITC jurisdiction (importation focus) and whether an exclusion remedy is an appropriate remedy to pursue or defend against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience representing both complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: We have both deep and recent experience representing both complainants and respondents in Section 337 cases before the ITC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should be able to handle either side's posture and understand offensive and defensive strategies, including differences in proving infringement/violations versus defending against exclusion and relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel proceeding strategy (pursue inter partes reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: We pursue parallel inter partes reviews (IPR) of the asserted patents to take advantage of more favorable standards in determining invalidity and to force the patent holder into taking positions that also compromise infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommended tactical criterion: coordinate IPRs with ITC litigation to leverage different invalidity standards and to extract concessions or positions from the patent owner that can aid the ITC defense or undermine infringement claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with co-pending district court and international actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations may be 'in a single matter or in conjunction with co-pending patent litigation matters' and can involve district court actions and foreign litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate counsel on ability to manage parallel litigation tracks (ITC, district courts, and foreign jurisdictions) as illustrated by examples involving multiple district court actions and litigations in Germany and the UK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs-stage and exclusion-order experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Our team has multiple and successful experiences at the customs stage of an investigation in ensuring that products are not excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expertise at the customs stage is essential for both securing enforcement of exclusion orders and defending clients against seizures or enforcement actions by U.S. Customs and Border Protection; counsel should have demonstrated customs-stage wins or strategies (e.g., Broadcom example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity and track record before ITC Administrative Law Judges (ALJs)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have appeared before each of the presiding Administrative Law Judges (ALJs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior appearances before the ALJs (and knowledge of their practices) are useful evaluative signals; counsel should demonstrate familiarity with ALJ procedures and preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability to handle high‑stakes ('bet the company') matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Our team has handled numerous high-profile 'bet the company' matters for both Complainants and Respondents at the ITC and knows how to drive successful resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select counsel with experience in high-risk, high-reward matters where the outcome could be company‑threatening; evaluate prior similar-scale matters and demonstrated outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proven outcomes: settlements, favorable decisions, and licensing results
rubrics_metrics.description: Client successes include a US$150M settlement, favorable ITC decisions leading to licensing, and multi-year licensing campaigns producing substantial revenue (e.g., over US$500M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete results (settlements, licensing income, successful enforcement/defense) as metrics when evaluating counsel effectiveness; consider examples cited (Spansion, HTC, Thomson, Rovi, Broadcom, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-border and multi-forum enforcement strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters have involved enforcement and litigation across venues (ITC, multiple district courts, Germany, UK) and integration of licensing campaigns with litigation strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate teams on their ability to integrate cross-border enforcement, coordinate parallel forum tactics, and translate ITC outcomes into licensing or settlement leverage internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and external recognition as proxy for expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition listed includes National Tier 1 rankings, inclusion in IAM Patent 1000, Benchmark Litigation, The American Lawyer, National Law Journal, and other awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rankings and external recognitions may be used as additional signals when selecting counsel, but should be weighed alongside concrete case outcomes and relevant ITC experience.
